title: The perfect locus with fixed degree
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and let $E\in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ be
perfect. Given $i,r\in\mathbb{Z}$ there is
an open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ characterized by the property: a
morphism $f:Y\to X$ factors through $U$ if and only if $Lf^*E$ is
isomorphic to a locally free $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module of rank $r$ placed in
degree $i$.

proof.text: For the general perfect-object formulation, if r<0 take the empty open. Otherwise work on each affine chart with a bounded finite projective representative supplied by def-pc-perfect-complex and make its finitely many terms free after shrinking using lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover. Shift the degree range to be nonnegative. When the prescribed degree lies below the lower bound, the required condition is empty if r>0, and is the acyclic locus if r=0; test it by the rank-zero single condition in degree 0. When the shifted prescribed degree is nonnegative, apply the following two steps in that degree. The locus so defined intrinsically by residue cohomology is independent of the chart and shift, so the resulting local opens glue. The Lean declaration in this delivery already starts with the nonnegative finite free representative and hence needs no preliminary chart or shift.

For the bounded nonnegative finite free representative P, define U to be the residue cohomology locus: all nonnegative cohomology other than i is zero and degree i is finite locally free of rank r. The lemma lem-pc-finite-free-residue-locus-open proves it is open by differential-rank inequalities; negative cohomology is zero by support.

For any g:Y\prime→Y, range(g)⊆U is precisely the universal residue condition over image points. Apply lem-pc-finite-free-pullback-residue-criterion to convert it to zero homology off i and finite locally free rank-r homology in degree i of g^*P. Package the two clauses in IsFiniteLocallyFreeInDegree. This is the complete Lean proof of IsFiniteFreeComplex.exists_opens_range_subset_iff; the general perfect-object statement is obtained on its local finite free representatives as in the original proof.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and let $P$ be a bounded complex of finite free
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules concentrated in degrees $[0,d]$, representing a
perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. Given integers $i,r\ge0$ there is
an open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ characterized by the property: a
morphism $f:Y\to X$ factors through $U$ if and only if
$Lf^*E=f^*P$ is isomorphic to a locally free $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module of
rank $r$ placed in degree $i$, that is, the cohomology sheaves
$H^q(f^*P)$ vanish for $q\neq i$ and $H^i(f^*P)$ is finite locally free
of rank $r$.

proof.text:
Since the terms of $P$ are free, hence flat, $f^*P$ computes $Lf^*E$
for every $f:Y\to X$ ([def-pc-perfect-complex]); and a complex whose
cohomology sheaves vanish outside degree $i$ is quasi-isomorphic to its
$i$-th cohomology sheaf placed in degree $i$, so the two descriptions of
the condition agree. Let $x\in X$ and let $M^\bullet$ be the restriction
of $P$ to a neighbourhood of $x$. Over the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, if a matrix of a differential
has a unit entry, row and column operations put that entry in a
$1\times1$ identity block. The equations $d^{j+1}d^j=0$ and
$d^jd^{j-1}=0$ force the adjacent maps into and out of this block
to be zero. Hence a contractible two-term summand splits off.
Each operation decreases the sum of the ranks of the terms by two,
so after finitely many operations the remaining complex has every
differential matrix in the maximal ideal.

Its residue-field differential is zero. Therefore, if
$H^j(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}\kappa(x))$ vanishes for $j\ne i$ and
has dimension $r$ in degree $i$, the remaining free terms have
rank zero except in degree $i$, where the rank is $r$.
All the changes of bases and the inverses of unit entries used in
this finite calculation are defined on an open neighbourhood of
$x$. On that neighbourhood $E$ is consequently quasi-isomorphic
to $\mathcal O^{\oplus r}[-i]$.

Define $U$ to be the set of points satisfying this residue-field
cohomology condition. The preceding construction proves that $U$
is open and that $E|_U$ is locally a free rank-$r$ module in degree
$i$. Such local descriptions agree on overlaps through the
cohomology sheaf $H^i(E)|_U$, which is therefore locally free of
rank $r$, with $E|_U\simeq H^i(E)|_U[-i]$.

If $f:Y\to X$ factors through $U$, these finite free descriptions
pull back to show that $Lf^*E$ has the required form. Conversely,
if $Lf^*E$ has that form, for any $y\in Y$ with image $x$ its
derived fibre equals
$(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}\kappa(x))\otimes_{\kappa(x)}\kappa(y)$.
Extension of fields is faithfully flat and preserves dimensions,
so $x$ satisfies exactly the defining condition of $U$. Thus the
image of $f$ is contained in $U$, which is equivalent to factoring
through that open subscheme.
